name: Dovetail
subcategory: feedback boards, interviews and product research
tagline: Store research notes, tag evidence, and create themes without recreating Dovetail's enterprise repos
verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Dovetail, store research notes, tag evidence, and create themes without recreating Dovetail's enterprise repository. The hard boundary is media transcription, participant data, integrations, governance, and collaboration scale, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Store research notes, tag evidence, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent research view without recreating Dovetail's enterprise repository.
whatYouLose: media transcription, participant data, integrations, governance, and collaboration scale
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Dovetail because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

alternatives.name: CATMA
alternatives.desc: Collaborative text annotation and analysis in a hosted academic tool, minus Dovetail's repository sprawl.

facts.install: Use the free hosted web app, or run the CATMA Standalone Docker image with its bundled GitLab backend
facts.dataFormat: The public service stores projects in CATMA's server-side GitLab repositories; standalone/self-hosted deployments keep CATMA and GitLab data in Docker volumes, with exports available as text, TEI-XML, CSV and Git repositories
facts.gapVsPaid: It supports collaborative text analysis, but not Dovetail's mixed-media research repository, transcription, stakeholder presentation, and enterprise collaboration.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted app is easy, but private/offline use means running a large Docker container with an embedded GitLab service and managing its volumes and updates

alternatives.name: QualCoder
alternatives.desc: Store evidence, code excerpts and build themes locally, without pretending it is an enterprise research hub.

facts.install: Windows installer/portable EXE or unsigned macOS DMG; Linux commonly runs the Python source or an Ubuntu release binary
facts.engines: Optional AI uses a local multilingual E5 sentence encoder and configurable LLMs including OpenAI GPT-4-class models, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google Gemini, Ollama and Blablador
facts.dataFormat: Each project is a folder containing imported media and a data.qda SQLite database; AI mode adds an ai_data folder with chat SQLite data and a local vector store
facts.gapVsPaid: It can code rich qualitative evidence locally, but it lacks Dovetail's cloud collaboration, repository search, polished sharing, and enterprise governance.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is platform packaging: Windows and macOS binaries are unsigned, while several Linux setups require Python source installation; VLC is also needed for audio/video coding

alternatives.name: Taguette
alternatives.desc: A focused repository for highlights, tags and exported findings; video-research polish is not invited.

facts.install: Free hosted signup, Windows EXE or macOS DMG, Linux pip install, or Docker for a self-hosted multi-user server
facts.dataFormat: Desktop projects and documents live in one local taguette.sqlite3 database; self-hosting can use SQLite or another SQLAlchemy database, while the free hosted service stores data on its server and encrypted off-site backups
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a focused highlight-and-tag repository, but video research, transcription, cross-project discovery, and polished stakeholder outputs are missing.
facts.setupBlocker: Windows and macOS packages install cleanly but are unsigned; Linux needs Python plus Calibre, and collaboration requires a configured server or the hosted service

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Team plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Dovetail in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: store research notes, tag evidence, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent research view without recreating Dovetail's enterprise repository.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
